slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In an indirect proof (proof by contradiction) we assume the opposite of what we want to prove and show that this leads to something impossible. Then the assumption must be false, so the statement is true.

Example: two different lines meet in at most one point. Suppose instead they meet in two points P and Q. Then two different lines would both pass through P and Q. That contradicts the postulate that exactly one line passes through two points. So they cannot meet in two points.
